_comment: Ashen Vale landform, read by Heightfield.from_dict. Metres, world XZ with the Mirror Pond at the origin. Layers compose in this order: noise hills -> valley-floor channel (calms the noise) -> pond basin -> boundary ridge -> plateaus. Slope targets: valley floor and routes <= 30 deg (player floor_max_angle is 45), ridge upper half > 45 so it reads as a wall.
_comment_holes: World XZ rects [x, z, w, h] where the terrain mesh AND collision are omitted so built structures can go underground. First: the castle crypt stairwell (tests/test_crypt_mouth.gd). Second: the stairwell down to the Hearth's chamber under the Mirror Pond, snapping to x -4..4, z -6..6 (tests/test_hearth_mouth.gd). Whatever is built must floor the SNAPPED hole, not the authored rect (D-014).

crests._comment: The wall round the hidden valley (W12): a ring of high ground with one gap in it. The gap is the only way in, which is the whole point of the place.
crests.name: hidden_ring

crests._comment: One of the two great hills the owner asked for (W16), sized to the ground that was actually free. A plateau cannot overlap a site, so these are as big as the valley had room for and no bigger.
crests.name: hill_1

crests._comment: One of the two great hills the owner asked for (W16), sized to the ground that was actually free. A plateau cannot overlap a site, so these are as big as the valley had room for and no bigger.
crests.name: hill_2

crests._comment: The shoulder over the Wide Water (W20). The owner asked for two cut hills with the river running between them at its widest; this is the north one. There is no south one, and saying so is better than pretending: the river runs within 60 m of the ridge clearance for most of its length and a hill on that side would stand outside the Vale. The gorge wall itself is 19 m deep in the north-east, which is the cut hill the request was really after.
crests.name: wide_water_shoulder

road._comment: The roads the terrain wears bare (W21-F). ONE polyline: the shader draws every consecutive pair of waypoints as a segment and holds at most TerrainMaterial.MAX_ROAD_SEGMENTS (8) of them, so a branch costs a double-back and nothing may be appended as a stray point -- the two points that were, after the castle and after Hollowmere, drew a 499 m track from the castle over the pond to Hollowmere's crofts and a second one back across the village to the Overlook. Read it in order: the Cutting's north-east mouth, its south-west mouth (the pair runs on the cut's own axis, between the two rock faces), the village plateau; the plateau out to Hollowmere's crofts and back (the spur, drawn twice, which is what a branch costs); then the old road, the valley polyline verbatim, plateau to crossroads to pond to the castle. Not fitted, because 8 is full: the castle to its own crossing (1 segment, but the gate is on the south side so it is really 3), and the Cutting on to Riverend (2 more). Those need the shader array raised to 12, or a road mask baked to a texture.

plateaus._comment: The islet in the Mirror Pond (W9-T): a stub of ground standing 2.6 m clear of the water for the broken light tower. Plateaus are applied after the basin is carved, which is what lets a rise sit inside the pond at all. It is set 28 m out on the perpendicular of the old road, so it crowds neither the pond seal at the centre nor the road that runs through the basin, and its skirt is long enough that the climb out of the water is walkable.
plateaus.name: isle

plateaus._comment: The Overlook (W11): high ground the player climbs to see the valley, asked for twice and finally built. It is 22 m up over a 57 m skirt, which is as big as the Vale had room for: a plateau cannot overlap a site, because its skirt would tilt the ground out from under one, and nothing in this valley had more than 87 m of clear space left. A watchtower stands on top so there is a reason to climb it.
plateaus.name: overlook

plateaus._comment: The floor of the hidden wood (W19). Two things decide every number here. The ground: the Vale's empty quarters are lumpy noise, 4 to 6 m of drop across any footprint, and nothing can stand on that -- so the floor is made flat, at 0.8 m, which is about the natural height here, so the skirt barely has to lean. And the neighbours: the nearest site is 53 m away and a skirt that reaches past it tilts the ground out from under it, so radius plus blend is 46 and no more. The first attempt at this stood in the south-east, where it tilted Castle Morrow's flat top from 125 m away; the castle's skirt is 158 m long and there is no room beside it.
plateaus.name: fellwood

waters._comment: The water itself, on exactly the line the cuts below dig for it: same points, same elevations. The surface and the bed cannot drift apart because they are the same numbers. W21: `half_width` is the channel (the map draws it); `spread` is how much further the SHEET runs out over the bank, equal to the cut's bank, so the water meets the ground wherever the sloping bank crosses the surface instead of stopping 10-20 m short of it on bare bed. The kill volume is as wide as the sheet but starts Water.WADE_DEPTH under the surface, so the shallows are wadeable and the bank is dry.
waters.name: river

waters._comment: The Wide Water's broader surface, over the broader cut. It shares its points with the river, so Water folds it into the river's one sheet (wider here) rather than drawing a second sheet on the same plane, which flickered.
waters.name: river_wide

cuts._comment: The river bed (W20). ABSOLUTE, not relative: the bed is cut to the water surface less `depth` whatever the ground was doing, and the ground is only ever lowered. The old river was a crest of fixed depth and the land along this line rises to +13 m, so the channel climbed with it while the water sat at -2.3 -- the owner filmed a river that was dry for 22 of its 31 steps, with the surface floating above sunken banks so you could walk underneath it. The surface falls from -4.2 m at the eastern rim to -7.5 m at the western one, a 0.4 % gradient over 863 m and never rises, so where the land is high the river runs in a gorge and where it is low it runs in a shallow trough.
cuts.name: river

cuts._comment: The Wide Water (W20): the middle reach, broader and deeper, which is where the owner asked for the river at its widest and a span hanging over it.
cuts.name: river_wide
